output.reason: This lens audits contract completeness, owner/root default-entry defects, transition-group guard collisions, and wrong-target/containment inconsistencies using cross-view exact bindings. Key findings: the collision-avoidance sub-machine (CollisionAvoidance) is never entered from root because the top-level model only wires [*] -> InitialState and provides no root edge into CollisionDetection or CollisionAvoidance; this defeats the NL2 initial-entry obligation into the active mode. The three activation events remain declared consumers on PossibleCollision inside CollisionDetection but no consumer transition is reachable from the root, defeating NL2 event-consumer coverage. The three activation-event alternatives are still structurally distinct (separate FrontendCollision/RearendCollision/PedestrianCollision targets tied 1:1 to distinct events), so no guard/event collision exists for the derived guard_disjointness contract; however, the entire group is unreachable, which is a distinct reachability property captured by the derived contract below, not a disjointness violation. The active-mode composite CollisionAvoidance retains 3 concurrent regions (braking/steering/alert) as required by NL3, and its state_action (concurrent activation) is structurally present via disjoint per-region entry edges, so NL3-REGION-1 and NL3-STATEACTION-1 are satisfied at the structural level, independent of the unreachability issue (which is captured only via the derived reachability contract, not by rewriting these). NL1 cardinality is handled purely through cardinality_bindings per instructions.

additional_contracts.normative_statement: The collision-avoidance sub-machine (CollisionAvoidance) and its upstream trigger scope (CollisionDetection) must be reachable from the model root so that the required activation behavior can actually occur; the closed FCSTM must not isolate the entire collision-detection/avoidance subsystem behind a root that never enters it.
additional_contracts.quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
additional_contracts.reason: NL2 requires the collision-avoidance sub-machine to become active upon detection events, which presupposes the sub-machine and its detection scope are reachable from the model root. The closed FCSTM's only root edge is '[*] -> InitialState' (fcstm_model.text, transition:line:62), and InitialState has no outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING at line:59). CollisionDetection and CollisionAvoidance are declared as sibling top-level states but have no incoming edge from root or from InitialState; verify_facts confirms reachability refuted for CollisionDetection (state:CollisionDetection:line:17) and CollisionAvoidance (state:CollisionAvoidance:line:31), and inspection_equivalent_facts.reachable_state_refs lists only the root wrapper and InitialState as reachable. This is a global topology defect distinct from the owner-local initial_entry contract (NL2-INITENTRY-1), which concerns CollisionAvoidance's own internal default entry; here the defect is that the entire CollisionAvoidance/CollisionDetection subsystem can never be entered from root at all, discharging the described activation obligation only as a candidate for the reachability property.
additional_contracts.scope: Root-to-collision-subsystem reachability required for the sub-machine activation obligation of NL2

response.reason: This lens prioritizes behavioral consequence: root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, owner entry, stable termination, and cross-wrapper reachability. The closed FCSTM shows the entire behavioral graph (CollisionDetection, CollisionAvoidance, OperationalControls and all their descendants) is unreachable from root: only llms_emp_feedback_final_0007 and InitialState are reachable_from_initial=true. This produces cascading consequence issues: the collision-avoidance activation obligation (NL2) cannot be entered because its owning composite is unreachable; the three collision-detection events cannot be consumed operationally although declared; the orthogonal-region behavior (NL3) cannot execute because CollisionAvoidance itself is unreachable; and InitialState itself is a reachable leaf with zero outgoing transitions, forming a genuine terminal sink that also breaks stable termination of the CollisionAvoidance->InitialState relation (that transition can never fire since CollisionAvoidance is unreachable, and even if it did, InitialState is a dead end with no re-entry to CollisionDetection, meaning the intended cyclic detection->avoidance->initial loop implied by the diagram's own transitions is severed at the root). I bind exact refs from inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts (reachable_from_initial=false for all descendant states; LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING for InitialState; EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for all 14 events). I derive one additional reachability contract for the collision-avoidance sub-machine's operating scope (CollisionAvoidance composite) since NL2's initial_entry contract is a narrower owner-local property that does not itself state the root-reachability defect; NL2-EVENTCOVER-1 gets a direct event_consumer_coverage candidate since the reachable_consumer sets are empty for all three named events despite declared consumers existing. NL3-REGION-1 and NL3-STATEACTION-1 are affected because the entire orthogonal-region owner is unreachable, so I derive a reachability obligation for that owner too, but I fold it into the same derived contract keyed to CollisionAvoidance since both NL2 and NL3 name the same owner scope (active mode of collision avoidance == CollisionAvoidance). NL1 cardinality is handled via cardinality_bindings only, no candidate. The guard_disjointness DERIVED-5fcc8fa8... contract is evaluated: since the three alternatives (frontend/rear-end/pedestrian) target three distinct states (FrontendCollision, RearendCollision, PedestrianCollision) rather than one shared CollisionAvoidanceActive target as the contract text assumed, they are already distinguishable by trigger and by target, so no guard_disjointness violation is evident from the closed model; I omit a candidate for it structurally distinguishable, but the deeper reachability defect (their common ancestor PossibleCollision is unreachable) is captured by the same derived reachability contract via event-consumer coverage failure, not via guard_disjointness, so I omit a separate candidate for the DERIVED contract in this lens and let the structural lens handle endpoint-level facts; I still emit the event-consumer coverage issue since that is the behavioral consequence.

This produces cascading consequence issues: the collision-avoidance activation obligation (NL2) cannot be entered because its owning composite is unreachable; the three collision-detection events cannot be consumed operationally although declared; the orthogonal-region behavior (NL3) cannot execute because CollisionAvoidance itself is unreachable; and InitialState itself is a reachable leaf with zero outgoing transitions, forming a genuine terminal sink that also breaks stable termination of the CollisionAvoidance->InitialState relation (that transition can never fire since CollisionAvoidance is unreachable, and even if it did, InitialState is a dead end with no re-entry to CollisionDetection, meaning the intended cyclic detection->avoidance->initial loop implied by the diagram's own transitions is severed at the root). I bind exact refs from inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts (reachable_from_initial=false for all descendant states; LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING for InitialState; EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for all 14 events). I derive one additional reachability contract for the collision-avoidance sub-machine's operating scope (CollisionAvoidance composite) since NL2's initial_entry contract is a narrower owner-local property that does not itself state the root-reachability defect; NL2-EVENTCOVER-1 gets a direct event_consumer_coverage candidate since the reachable_consumer sets are empty for all three named events despite declared consumers existing. NL3-REGION-1 and NL3-STATEACTION-1 are affected because the entire orthogonal-region owner is unreachable, so I derive a reachability obligation for that owner too, but I fold it into the same derived contract keyed to CollisionAvoidance since both NL2 and NL3 name the same owner scope (active mode of collision avoidance == CollisionAvoidance). NL1 cardinality is handled via cardinality_bindings only, no candidate. The guard_disjointness DERIVED-5fcc8fa8... contract is evaluated: since the three alternatives (frontend/rear-end/pedestrian) target three distinct states (FrontendCollision, RearendCollision, PedestrianCollision) rather than one shared CollisionAvoidanceActive target as the contract text assumed, they are already distinguishable by trigger and by target, so no guard_disjointness violation is evident from the closed model; I omit a candidate for it structurally distinguishable, but the deeper reachability defect (their common ancestor PossibleCollision is unreachable) is captured by the same derived reachability contract via event-consumer coverage failure, not via guard_disjointness, so I omit a separate candidate for the DERIVED contract in this lens and let the structural lens handle endpoint-level facts; I still emit the event-consumer coverage issue since that is the behavioral consequence.

result.reason: This lens prioritizes behavioral consequence: root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, owner entry, stable termination, and cross-wrapper reachability. The closed FCSTM shows the entire behavioral graph (CollisionDetection, CollisionAvoidance, OperationalControls and all their descendants) is unreachable from root: only llms_emp_feedback_final_0007 and InitialState are reachable_from_initial=true. This produces cascading consequence issues: the collision-avoidance activation obligation (NL2) cannot be entered because its owning composite is unreachable; the three collision-detection events cannot be consumed operationally although declared; the orthogonal-region behavior (NL3) cannot execute because CollisionAvoidance itself is unreachable; and InitialState itself is a reachable leaf with zero outgoing transitions, forming a genuine terminal sink that also breaks stable termination of the CollisionAvoidance->InitialState relation (that transition can never fire since CollisionAvoidance is unreachable, and even if it did, InitialState is a dead end with no re-entry to CollisionDetection, meaning the intended cyclic detection->avoidance->initial loop implied by the diagram's own transitions is severed at the root). I bind exact refs from inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts (reachable_from_initial=false for all descendant states; LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING for InitialState; EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for all 14 events). I derive one additional reachability contract for the collision-avoidance sub-machine's operating scope (CollisionAvoidance composite) since NL2's initial_entry contract is a narrower owner-local property that does not itself state the root-reachability defect; NL2-EVENTCOVER-1 gets a direct event_consumer_coverage candidate since the reachable_consumer sets are empty for all three named events despite declared consumers existing. NL3-REGION-1 and NL3-STATEACTION-1 are affected because the entire orthogonal-region owner is unreachable, so I derive a reachability obligation for that owner too, but I fold it into the same derived contract keyed to CollisionAvoidance since both NL2 and NL3 name the same owner scope (active mode of collision avoidance == CollisionAvoidance). NL1 cardinality is handled via cardinality_bindings only, no candidate. The guard_disjointness DERIVED-5fcc8fa8... contract is evaluated: since the three alternatives (frontend/rear-end/pedestrian) target three distinct states (FrontendCollision, RearendCollision, PedestrianCollision) rather than one shared CollisionAvoidanceActive target as the contract text assumed, they are already distinguishable by trigger and by target, so no guard_disjointness violation is evident from the closed model; I omit a candidate for it structurally distinguishable, but the deeper reachability defect (their common ancestor PossibleCollision is unreachable) is captured by the same derived reachability contract via event-consumer coverage failure, not via guard_disjointness, so I omit a separate candidate for the DERIVED contract in this lens and let the structural lens handle endpoint-level facts; I still emit the event-consumer coverage issue since that is the behavioral consequence.

decisions.reason: NL2 requires that 'this sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.' The exact activation edge CollisionDetection->CollisionAvoidance (transition:line:60) is structurally present, but CollisionDetection itself is unreachable from root per the sole top-level edge '[*]->InitialState' (transition:line:62); verify_facts refutes reachability for both states. branches.reason: This lens prioritizes behavioral consequence: root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, owner entry, stable termination, and cross-wrapper reachability. The closed FCSTM shows the entire behavioral graph (CollisionDetection, CollisionAvoidance, OperationalControls and all their descendants) is unreachable from root: only llms_emp_feedback_final_0007 and InitialState are reachable_from_initial=true. This produces cascading consequence issues: the collision-avoidance activation obligation (NL2) cannot be entered because its owning composite is unreachable; the three collision-detection events cannot be consumed operationally although declared; the orthogonal-region behavior (NL3) cannot execute because CollisionAvoidance itself is unreachable; and InitialState itself is a reachable leaf with zero outgoing transitions, forming a genuine terminal sink that also breaks stable termination of the CollisionAvoidance->InitialState relation (that transition can never fire since CollisionAvoidance is unreachable, and even if it did, InitialState is a dead end with no re-entry to CollisionDetection, meaning the intended cyclic detection->avoidance->initial loop implied by the diagram's own transitions is severed at the root). I bind exact refs from inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts (reachable_from_initial=false for all descendant states; LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING for InitialState; EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for all 14 events). I derive one additional reachability contract for the collision-avoidance sub-machine's operating scope (CollisionAvoidance composite) since NL2's initial_entry contract is a narrower owner-local property that does not itself state the root-reachability defect; NL2-EVENTCOVER-1 gets a direct event_consumer_coverage candidate since the reachable_consumer sets are empty for all three named events despite declared consumers existing. NL3-REGION-1 and NL3-STATEACTION-1 are affected because the entire orthogonal-region owner is unreachable, so I derive a reachability obligation for that owner too, but I fold it into the same derived contract keyed to CollisionAvoidance since both NL2 and NL3 name the same owner scope (active mode of collision avoidance == CollisionAvoidance). NL1 cardinality is handled via cardinality_bindings only, no candidate. The guard_disjointness DERIVED-5fcc8fa8... contract is evaluated: since the three alternatives (frontend/rear-end/pedestrian) target three distinct states (FrontendCollision, RearendCollision, PedestrianCollision) rather than one shared CollisionAvoidanceActive target as the contract text assumed, they are already distinguishable by trigger and by target, so no guard_disjointness violation is evident from the closed model; I omit a candidate for it structurally distinguishable, but the deeper reachability defect (their common ancestor PossibleCollision is unreachable) is captured by the same derived reachability contract via event-consumer coverage failure, not via guard_disjointness, so I omit a separate candidate for the DERIVED contract in this lens and let the structural lens handle endpoint-level facts; I still emit the event-consumer coverage issue since that is the behavioral consequence.
